published_sources.title: A grid-based methodology for fast online changepoint detection
published_sources.author: Per August Jarval Moen
published_sources.published_claim_scope: For a broad compatible class of statistics, dynamically updated sparse grids give at-most-logarithmic update/storage growth and translate offline finite-sample power into online delay bounds under a robustness condition; mean/covariance special cases receive near-optimal non-asymptotic delay bounds.

published_sources.title: gridcp: Fast Online Changepoint Detection in Python
published_sources.published_claim_scope: Open-source implementation of the geometric-grid methodology with nine built-in test families, custom-score support and Monte Carlo threshold calibration.

package_repository.main_vs_release: one README-only commit ahead; source/tests unchanged by that comparison

paper_reproduction_repository.declared_setup: pip install gridcp==0.1.0 jupyter matplotlib numpy pandas
paper_reproduction_repository.paper_material_claim: README states each notebook reproduces one figure or timing result; included data cover the GRB/simulation inputs and the well-log notebook downloads TCPD data on first run.
paper_reproduction_repository.exactness_note: README states N_JOBS=18 is required for exact simulation reproducibility.
limitations_observed: No full dependency lock/environment file beyond pinning gridcp==0.1.0.
Inspected notebooks store execution_count=null and empty outputs, so repository state does not archive the numerical outputs to compare against a rerun.
Simulation notebooks are declared to require substantial compute; the FAR notebook uses 20,000 calibration paths and 100,000 null paths to length 10,000.
Notebook metadata reports Python 3.14.4 whereas package CI observed here covers Python 3.10 and 3.13; this is an environment provenance mismatch, not evidence of a numerical error.

independent_mechanical_checks.method: Reimplemented the exact public get_G_grid formula and recursive grid-update logic from the observed package source in an independent Python criterion harness; this checks the geometric-retention mechanism itself, not the paper's full detection-delay simulation.
results: Recursive grid update matched the non-recursive t-G construction for every t=1..100000.
Recycling property G(t+1)\{1}-1 subseteq G(t) held for every t=1..99999.
The geometric coverage criterion d/2 <= g <= d for some g in G(t), for each d<=t/2, had no violation in exhaustive checks through t=5000 and 20,000 additional random (t,d) probes with t<=1,000,000.

At t=100000 the retained grid size was 32; over t<=100000 the maximum observed |G(t)|/ln(t) was about 2.796, consistent with the published <3 ln(t) type bound. Selected sizes were 18 at t=1000, 25 at t=10000 and 38 at t=1000000.
independent_mechanical_checks.scope: These are independent implementation-criterion checks of grid shape, recycling and logarithmic retained-state growth. They do not independently reproduce the paper's false-alarm calibration, timing benchmark, finite-sample power curves, or theorem proofs.

independent_replication_search.search_scope: Fresh exact-title/package/reproduction searches plus GitHub repository discovery during this invocation found the official package/paper repositories but no genuinely independent same-protocol numerical rerun.
independent_replication_search.interpretation: Absence of a located independent rerun is not evidence that none exists.

assessment.overall_grade: A- for geometric-grid mechanism reproducibility; B+ for official paper-level reproducibility; C for the worker's e-detector transfer
assessment.reasoning: The exact geometric-grid implementation is public, version-tagged, heavily tested, and CI-clean at the release commit. A separate reproduction repository pins the package version and supplies six paper notebooks plus data. Independent criterion checks reproduced the grid's recursive/nonrecursive identity, recycling property, geometric coverage and logarithmic retained-state behavior. However the paper repository does not archive executed notebook outputs or a fully locked environment, and no independent same-protocol numerical rerun was located. Most importantly, none of this validates the worker's proposed transfer of the grid to a non-partitioned e-detector: that transfer still needs a separate false-alarm-validity and delay proof/experiment.

downstream_scope_guard.safe_positive_statement: Moen's geometric-grid retention mechanism is strongly implementation-supported and independently criterion-checked for recycling, coverage and logarithmic retained-state growth.
downstream_scope_guard.unsafe_overclaim: Do not treat gridcp or Moen's theorem as proof that the Saha-Ramdas non-partitioned e-detector preserves ARL/PFA validity or first-order/non-asymptotic delay after geometric start sparsification.
required_transfer_evidence: Prove the retained e-detector is pathwise bounded by or otherwise preserves the full detector's false-alarm validity under the exact subset construction.
Map the grid nearest-split/lag guarantee to the two-start unknown-baseline delay argument with explicit constants and scope.
Run matched stopping-time simulations against the full all-start e-detector, including weak-change regimes and the outer candidate-null optimization cost.
